name: UserList.__init__
note: review: `ulNew` merges the exact `type(initlist) == type(self.data)` test (:1292) with the isinstance sense of `.list`, so a list subclass, which goes through `list(initlist)` and its `__iter__`, is not distinguished; `.iter ty l` is pre-materialised, so an iterator that raises cannot occur; and with no identity, an `__init__` that aliased `initlist` instead of copying it (`self.data[:] = initlist`) passes the rfl conjuncts of UserListOperandsAgree.

name: UserList.__repr__
note: review: `ListOps.repr : List α → String` can neither raise nor recurse, so an element `__repr__` that raises and the `[...]` of a UserList that holds itself cannot be expressed, and UserListObservers states only `ulRepr ops u = ops.repr u.data`, the definition (UserDict.__repr__ pins both cases).

name: UserList.__lt__
note: review: `ListOps.rich` returns an infallible `Bool`, but list comparison returns the result of the first differing pair's `<`, which can be any object, and an element `__eq__` can raise; `ulCmp` fixes a non-list operand to TypeError without trying its reflected `__gt__`; the theorems only restate `ulCmp = ops.rich` and, on ints, that `l < l` is false.

name: UserList.__le__
note: review: As `__lt__`: the `Bool`-valued, infallible `rich` cannot hold the element comparison's object or its exception, and a non-list operand's reflected `__ge__` is never tried; on ints only `l <= l` is checked.

name: UserList.__eq__
note: review: `ulCmp` fixes `==` against a non-list operand to `False`, but `self.data == other` then calls the operand's reflected `__eq__` (`UserList([1]) == unittest.mock.ANY` is True); `rich` is an infallible `Bool`, though element `__eq__` can raise or return any object; on ints only reflexivity is checked.

name: UserList.__gt__
note: review: As `__lt__`, with only UserListOperandsAgree's restatement `ulCmp = ops.rich` and no statement at all on a non-list operand.

name: UserList.__ge__
note: review: As `__gt__`: the infallible `Bool` `rich` cannot hold the element comparison's result or its exception, and the reflected `__le__` of a non-list operand is not modelled.

name: UserList.__cast
note: review: `ulCast` mirrors :1317-1318, but no theorem states `ulCmp` on an `.iter` or `.noniter` operand, so a `__cast` that turned any iterable into a list (making `UserList([1]) == (1,)` true) passes UserListOperandsAgree; its docstring also cites `__cast` at :1266-1267, which is UserDict code in 3.15.2.

name: UserList.__contains__
note: review: `ListOps.contains : List α → α → Bool` cannot raise, so an element `__eq__` that raises inside `item in self.data` cannot be expressed, and the conjunct is the rfl definition.

name: UserList.__add__
note: review: The three branches are mirrored, but `.iter ty l` is an already-materialised list, so `list(other)` failing part way (an `__iter__` or `__next__` that raises) cannot be expressed; only the non-iterable TypeError is.

name: UserList.__radd__
note: review: As `__add__`: `list(other)` on a raising iterator is not expressible, since `.iter` holds the items already read.

name: UserList.__iadd__
note: review: `.iter` is pre-materialised, so the one observable difference of this body cannot be expressed: `self.data += list(other)` leaves `u` unchanged when the iterator raises part way, while `list.__iadd__` and `UserList.extend` keep the items already read; UserListOperandsAgree's `ulIadd = ulExtend` would be false there, and UserListSimulatesList drives `+=` with list operands only.
